cur:catacombs2-callixtus-pecorelle-good-.summary: In this lunette above a tomb, the Good Shepherd stands at the centre among his sheep, which turn towards figures who make water flow, perhaps Moses striking the rock, so that the flock may drink. The slide's caption calls it the 'Good Shepherd and the outpouring of the waters of grace': Christ the shepherd gathers his flock to the living water of baptism.
facts: The chamber takes its popular name, 'delle Pecorelle' (of the little sheep), from this painting.
The Leuven record dates it to the second half of the 4th century and cites Wilpert, plate 235, while the slide label dates it to the early 4th century.
cur:catacombs2-callixtus-pecorelle-good-.notes: The centre of the lunette is cut by a later loculus; the side figures are partly obscured and their identification is uncertain.

walters:48.2632.summary: Stamped reliefs are spaced across the floor of this red earthenware bowl. At the top stands Lazarus' tomb, a small temple-like shrine on a decorated base with the swaddled Lazarus upright in its doorway. A veiled woman stands at the left, and at the right a long-haired figure in a mantle stretches out a hand towards the tomb in a gesture of command, generally read as Christ calling his friend back to life; two small trees complete the scene.
facts: The Walters explains that the bowl belongs to a group of stamped terracotta objects made in North Africa as an inexpensive substitute for vessels of precious metal.
The Raising of Lazarus was one of the most popular subjects in the Roman catacombs, appearing from the 2nd century.
walters:48.2632.notes: Identification uncertain: the gesturing figure at the right lacks the wand usually held by Christ in this scene and could be read as one of Lazarus' sisters; the museum text does not identify the figures.
